verdict: FAIL (5.5 < 7.5). The revision is unusually honest and internally consistent: spot-checked headline numbers (D = 0.4168, refined-grid D values, matched-slip interpolations, H2b, H4e, LTT) all recompute correctly from the reported arm-level RE and frontier points, and every limitation is disclosed. But the disclosures themselves expose a thin core contribution. The 'certificate' needs simulator replays and so exists only in simulation. The onset noise that sets the effect size is assumed, not measured. The validity premise failed, so the primary route was adopted after that failure. The learned model, the paper's most elaborate component, shows no demonstrated gain over a one-line plug-in. The tactile competitors that matter (reactive slip tightening, friction estimation with a tuned per-stratum margin) were not run. The 'minimal-force' saving applies only to the hold force after a fixed ~49 N peak protocol that exceeds most objects' minimal holding force. Of four pre-registered core decisions, one is confirmed. The prose is also overloaded with hedges and numbers, which makes the paper hard to read. Several gaps can be closed from existing replays without new simulation; others need new experiments.
strengths: Exemplary transparency: pre-registration, deviations (Appendix B), a hypothesis ledger, failed and inconclusive decisions, and a sub-pool in which the method loses are all reported plainly.

Numerical internal consistency: the headline and secondary D values, matched-slip RE values and the LTT contrast recompute exactly from the reported arm-level RE and slip and the frontier points across the text, tables and Figure 1.

Sound statistical design for the main contrast: comparator chosen on a disjoint selection split before calibration/test data were read; object-cluster bootstrap that recomputes lambda-hat in every draw; Bonferroni across core decisions; SESOI and F*_lo/F*_hi sensitivity.

Clean protocol design that isolates the friction channel (friction-uninformative fixed preload; friction drawn independently of all non-tactile inputs), enabling a clear attribution: the probe carries the information and a physics plug-in on the onset captures most of the saving.

Careful scoping of the guarantee: marginal, in-expectation, per stratum, simulation-only; LTT reported as per-stratum with the union-bound caveat; online tracking's slip level correctly framed as an accounting identity rather than a finding.
Noise-sensitivity curve (sigma = 0 to 0.4) and the CSF-proxy sweep give readers the conditions under which the effect holds or vanishes.
weaknesses: [evidence-level] Simulation only, with a modelled detector and an assumed onset noise sigma = 0.2 that sets the effect size (D falls from 0.68 to 0.14 over sigma 0 to 0.4). No sensor measurement or hardware data anchors where a real gripper sits on that curve.

[evidence-level] The offline certificate, the paper's titular contribution, needs replays of each calibration grasp at every grid force, so it cannot be used on a robot. The deployable route (online tracking with physical feedback) is descriptive only: 5 orderings, S1/S3 only, no intervals, post-shift transient window omitted.

[evidence-level] No tactile competitors. Reactive slip-detect-and-tighten controllers and friction-estimate controllers with a tuned per-stratum margin are the natural baselines, and the paper concedes it cannot claim to beat existing tactile grip control at equal slip. The only tactile stand-in (uniform fixed margin) is weak by construction.

[evidence-level] The 'minimal-force' framing is undercut by the fixed protocol: a 32.7 N preload and a ~49 N squeeze peak on every object exceed most objects' minimal holding force, and the probe induces micro-slip on every grasp. Absolute newtons, peak force, integrated force and the F* distribution are not reported, and there is no adaptive-preload variant, so the practical value of a 42% relative hold-force saving cannot be judged.

[evidence-level] The learned model's role is unresolved. The registered H2b estimate is biased by the plug-in's grid floor; TOST equivalence is met on neither CRC grid; no direct learned-vs-plug-in contrast was computed at matched slip or under LTT; and the shrunk plug-in that would test the shrinkage explanation was not run.

[evidence-level] Validity premise (H1) failed, and the CRC route and refined grid were adopted post hoc. Realised per-stratum slip exceeds alpha in several strata and for one predictor seed. The certificate was checked on a single calibration/test split, with no repeated object re-splits, even though these need no new simulation.

[evidence-level] The sub-pool reversal (D = -0.2614) rests on the label route, whose premise failed, with about 88 calibration grasps per stratum. Arm-level RE and slip are not reported, narrow friction is confounded with mid-amplitude, and a CRC re-run from existing replays was not done.

[evidence-level] Multiplicity: the registered Holm correction for secondary families was dropped, and no adjusted values are reported, so several secondary superiority labels and the reversal carry no family-wise control.

[evidence-level] The online efficiency decision (H3) is inconclusive and underpowered (realised half-widths 0.15 to 0.20 against a projected 0.12). The oracle reference itself slips above alpha in S2, and the slip-matching co-requirement fails in S1 and S2.

[paper-level] Novelty is modest as framed: probing friction from incipient slip is established, and CRC, LTT and quantile tracking are used as published. The contribution reduces to a protocol plus an attribution study in simulation, and the title's 'Certified' oversells it given the failed validity premise and simulation-only replays.

[paper-level] Readability: the abstract, contributions, Section 5 and Figure 1 are saturated with numbers, route labels and nested caveats (e.g., the Section 5.2 learned-vs-plug-in paragraph and the abstract's sub-pool sentence). The main message is hard to extract, and the headline caveats are repeated in the intro, Section 6, Section 7 and Section 8.

[paper-level] Presentation defects: Tables 4 and 5 appear before Tables 1 to 3. Figure 1 has three dense panels plus an inset and footnotes. Per-stratum refined-grid slips are described as 'not tabulated in our results index' but recomputed, a provenance remark that does not belong in a paper. Ledger codes (H2a, A1, B2) still dominate the tables even though the text says it uses descriptive names.
required_actions: [evidence-level] Ground sigma: measure onset-detection noise on a physical gripper with a real tactile sensor (even a small object set), or at minimum calibrate the simulated detector against published incipient-slip detection error, and place the headline on the sigma curve accordingly.

[evidence-level] Add the natural tactile baselines at matched slip: a reactive slip-detect-and-tighten controller and a friction-estimate controller (e.g., the CSF-mu-hat force) with a per-stratum margin tuned on the selection split. Report whether probe + CRC beats them in force at equal realised slip.

[evidence-level] Report force accounting per arm: absolute excess hold force in N, peak force, integrated force over the protocol plus a representative hold duration, and the distribution of F*_mid relative to F0. Ideally add an adaptive or lower preload variant so the minimal-force claim is not dominated by the protocol.

[evidence-level] Resolve the learned-vs-plug-in question: run a shrunk plug-in (onset estimate shrunk towards the population friction, with shrinkage set on the selection split) and compute direct CertGrip-full vs CSF-mu-hat contrasts at matched slip and under LTT on the refined grid.

[evidence-level, no new simulation] Run repeated object-level calibration/test re-splits from the existing replays and report the distribution of realised per-stratum slip and of D. Tabulate per-stratum slip on both grids, plus conditional slip per family x stratum and per friction quintile.

[evidence-level, no new simulation] Re-run the narrow-friction sub-pool on the CRC route from the existing replays. Report arm-level RE and slip, and de-confound the narrow-friction and mid-amplitude restrictions (run each restriction separately).
[evidence-level, no new simulation] Report Holm-adjusted p-values or intervals for the secondary families as registered, alongside the unadjusted ones.

[evidence-level] Strengthen the deployable route: physical-feedback online streams with all three shifts, 20 orderings, bootstrap intervals and the post-shift transient window (steps 501 to 1,000) reported, ideally against an oracle that is itself valid in S2.

[paper-level] Reframe the title and contributions so 'certified' is visibly qualified as simulation-only and conditional. Present the contribution honestly as a probe protocol plus a calibrated plug-in plus an attribution study, and demote the learned model.

[paper-level] Cut the density: shorten the abstract to the headline, its two key conditions (sigma and friction range) and the deployability caveat. State each caveat once (Limitations), with brief pointers elsewhere. Move secondary route-by-route numbers from the Section 5.2 prose into tables.

[paper-level] Fix the presentation: number the tables in order of appearance, simplify Figure 1 (fewer annotations; move the inset or the sub-pool footnote into the caption or the text), remove the 'results index / recomputation' provenance language by tabulating the numbers, and use descriptive row names in the main-text tables.
